# Model Benchmark & Selection

**Date:** 1 September 2026
**Runtime profile of all measurements below:** `DEV_CPU` — Apple Silicon arm64, 10 vCPU, **no CUDA GPU**
**Corpus of all measurements below:** `LOCAL SYNTHETIC CORPUS` (6 cameras, generated by `tools/sandbox/`)

> **Measurement class.** Every number produced by us is labelled **MEASURED** and
> is valid only for the corpus and hardware named above. It is a *regression and
> comparison* number, not field accuracy. Publisher figures are labelled
> **REPORTED** and attributed. No GPU figure in this document is measured,
> because no GPU has been available — those are labelled **MODELLED**.

---

## 1. Selection summary

| Task | Selected | Licence | Status | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plate detect + OCR | `anpr-onnx-cpu@1.0.0` | MIT | **ACTIVE**, demo-approved | MEASURED |
| Plate detect (alt) | `plate-rtdetrv2@0.1.0` | Apache-2.0 | CANDIDATE | not yet benchmarked |
| Indian OCR | `ocr-awiros-india@0.1.0` | Apache-2.0 | CANDIDATE | REPORTED only |
| Vehicle detect | `vehicle-rtdetrv2-r18@0.1.0` | Apache-2.0 | CANDIDATE | not yet benchmarked |
| Appearance embed | `embed-dinov2-base@0.1.0` | Apache-2.0 | CANDIDATE | not yet benchmarked |
| Forensic VLM | `vlm-qwen3-vl-4b@0.1.0` | Apache-2.0 | CANDIDATE, GPU-only | unavailable on DEV_CPU |

Nothing is approved for **production**. Production approval requires measurement
on real Indian CCTV footage, which we do not have.

## 2. Measured: plate detection + OCR

`tools/benchmark_models/run.py --task plate_detect_ocr --fps 2 --include-rejected`

| Model | Licence | Recall | Char acc | p50 ms | FPS | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `anpr-onnx-cpu@1.0.0` | MIT | **0.83** | 0.53 | 62 | 13.0 | **Selected** |
| `anpr-onnx-fastalpr-default@0.0.0` | MIT | **0.00** | 0.00 | 26 | 25.4 | **Rejected** |

The rejected row is the configuration you get by accepting `fast-alpr`'s
defaults. It is twice as fast and reads **nothing correctly**, because its OCR
head has `max_plate_slots = 9` and a standard Indian registration mark is 10
characters. It does not fail loudly — it returns confident truncations such as
`GJ05AB1` for `GJ05AB1234`. Benchmarking it deliberately is what turns "we chose
a different model" into evidence.

### Per-camera detail (4 fps run, `var/logs/anpr_eval.json`)

| Camera | Department | Resolution | Recall | Read | ms/frame |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C-052 | Health | 960×540 | 1.00 | `GJ27PQ7788` | 64 |
| C-061 | Police | 1280×720 | 1.00 | `GJ05AB9999` | 67 |
| C-047 | Municipal | 1920×1080 | 0.50 | `GJ05AB1234` | 90 |
| C-014 | Traffic | 1280×720 | 0.33 | `GJ18XY9012` | 67 |
| C-021 | GSRTC | 1280×720 | 0.33 | `GJ06MN3344` | 75 |
| **C-033** | **Panchayat** | **640×480** | **0.00** | **declined** | 67 |

**0 false positives across all cameras.** C-033 is the degraded camera; it
produced 1 detection and 0 format-valid reads across 200 frames and the system
declined rather than guessing. The 0.33 recalls on C-014 and C-021 are a known
limitation, not a model failure: without a tracker every vehicle on a camera
shares one voting bucket and the 12-second window prunes earlier vehicles. The
tracker resolves it.

### Three findings that changed the selection

1. **Resolution must be normalised before detection.** A 1920×1080 frame gave
   **0 detections**; the identical frame downscaled to 1280×720, 960×540 or
   640×360 gave the same plate at **0.66**. On a heterogeneous estate this means
   a camera's resolution silently decides whether ANPR works at all.
2. **The tiny model beat the small model.** `yolo-v9-t-640` scored **0.83–0.86**
   where `yolo-v9-s-608` scored **0.30–0.44** on identical frames. Input
   resolution dominates parameter count for objects this small.
3. **OCR slot count is a hard structural ceiling**, not an accuracy gradient.
   9 slots cannot represent a 10-character mark under any threshold.

## 3. Hugging Face survey

Surveyed via the HF API on 1 September 2026. Ranked by measured suitability, not
downloads — the most-downloaded option in two of these categories is unusable.

### Plate detection

| Model | Licence | DL | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `morsetechlab/yolov11-license-plate-detection` | **AGPL-3.0** | 68,237 | **Rejected on licence.** Most-downloaded, therefore the default trap. |
| `Koushim/yolov8-license-plate-detection` | MIT (declared) | 43,371 | **Avoid.** YOLOv8 derivative; an MIT tag on Ultralytics-derived weights is not a licence we would defend to a government buyer. |
| `justjuu/rtdetr-v2-license-plate-detection` | Apache-2.0 | 840 | **Candidate.** Licence-clean, transformers-native. `rev 0ca7598f5864`. |
| `open-image-models` yolo-v9-t-640 | MIT | — | **In use.** Not on the Hub; ships with the MIT package. |

### Plate OCR (Indian)

| Model | Licence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `Awiros/anpr-ocr` | Apache-2.0 | **Highest-value candidate.** `rev eadbc5ae4faa`, 149 MB `model.safetensors`, PP-OCRv5 architecture, ships a technical report. REPORTED 98.42% on Indian plates (98.83% single-row, 96.91% dual-row) — **not verified by us**. Handles **dual-row** plates, which every generic model fails. Needs PaddlePaddle or an ONNX export, so it is not a drop-in. |
| `cct-s-v2-global-model` | MIT | **In use.** 10 slots, generic. |
| `global-plates-mobile-vit-v2-model` | MIT | **Rejected.** 9 slots. |

### Vehicle detection

| Model | Licence | DL | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PekingU/rtdetr_v2_r18vd` | Apache-2.0 | 405,774 | **Primary candidate.** 81 MB, `rev 5650961749fa`, COCO classes give car/motorcycle/bus/truck directly. |
| `Roboflow/rf-detr-base` | Apache-2.0 | 37,401 | Alternative, 129 MB. Likely GPU-tier. |
| Ultralytics YOLO (any) | **AGPL-3.0** | — | **Rejected on licence.** |

### Vehicle Re-ID — the honest finding

**There is no credible off-the-shelf vehicle Re-ID model on the Hub.** Every
task-specific candidate found has **zero downloads** and no published
evaluation:

| Model | Licence | DL |
|---|---|---|
| `occurra/vehicle_reid_siglip2_naflex_512d` | Apache-2.0 | 0 |
| `umair894/KAT-ReID-Veri776` | Apache-2.0 | 0 |
| `occurra/vehicle_vit_clip_reid` | MIT | 0 |

Decision: use a **general-purpose embedder as the baseline** —
`facebook/dinov2-base` (Apache-2.0, 2.8M downloads, `rev f9e44c814b77`) — and
only adopt a task-specific model if our own harness shows it beats that baseline
on Recall@K. A strong, widely-validated general embedder with a known licence is
more defensible in front of a technical jury than an unproven task-specific one
with no users.

`facebook/dinov3-vitb16` was considered and set aside: its licence is `other`,
not Apache-2.0.

### Vehicle attributes

The HF search returned **nothing usable** for vehicle colour or make/model
classification. Plan: colour from classical CV on the vehicle crop (cheap,
explainable, no licence risk), type from the detector's COCO class. This is a
case where a model is not the right answer.

## 4. Execution profiles

| | `DEV_CPU` | `CLOUD_GPU` | `TARGET_GPU` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Purpose | correctness, regression | benchmarking, accuracy | deployment |
| Providers | `CPUExecutionProvider` | CUDA → CPU | TensorRT → CUDA → CPU |
| Heavy models (>500 MB) | blocked | allowed | allowed |
| Forensic VLM | unavailable | available | available |
| Mandatory chain (plate → route → alert) | **works** | works | works |

Enforced by tests: `test_every_profile_can_run_the_mandatory_chain` asserts that
no profile can make plate reading impossible, and
`test_gpu_profile_is_refused_without_a_gpu` asserts that requesting a GPU profile
on a CPU host **falls back and says so** rather than silently pretending — any
timing recorded there is CPU timing and must not be presented otherwise.

CoreML is detected on this hardware but **excluded by default**: it fails on
graphs with zero-element dynamic shapes, which was observed taking down the whole
plate-detection call. Opt in with `SAAKSHYA_ENABLE_COREML=1` per graph.

---

## 5. What is not measured

Stated plainly so no one quotes these by accident:

- **No GPU latency or throughput has been measured.** Every GPU figure anywhere
  in this project is MODELLED.
- **No accuracy on real CCTV footage.** The corpus is synthetic, and synthetic
  plates are cleaner than real ones — high-contrast, fronto-parallel, no motion
  blur beyond what we inject. Real-world accuracy will be **lower**.
- **No Re-ID, vehicle-detection or VLM benchmark yet.** Those models are
  registered as CANDIDATE with no measurement.
- **The Awiros Indian OCR figure is the publisher's**, not ours.

## 6. Reproducing

```bash
make sandbox
python tools/benchmark_models/run.py --task plate_detect_ocr --fps 2 --include-rejected
python tests/evaluation/run_anpr_eval.py --fps 4
```

Outputs land in `var/logs/benchmark/` as `.json`, `.csv` and `.md`, each stamped
with the runtime profile and hardware summary.
